section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei,
Yud Kislev 5746*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" was recited by Dovid and by several Rebbes on their respective redemption days.
section.t: "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, for many were with me."
And it is known,
that in addition to the simple meaning of the matter, that this verse was said by Dovid regarding his own redemption,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, redeemed him from the wars that came upon him,
this verse also alludes to the redemption of several tzaddikim,
and certainly the redemption of the tzaddikim who said this verse at the time they were redeemed.
And it is noteworthy,
that in all three redemptions of our Nesi'im — the redemption of the Alter Rebbe on Yud-Tes Kislev,
the redemption of the Mitteler Rebbe on Yud Kislev,
and the redemption of my father-in-law, the Rebbe, on Yud-Beis Tammuz — the masters of the redemption said this verse on the day they were redeemed.
Regarding the redemption of the Alter Rebbe on Yud-Tes Kislev, it is known what the Alter Rebbe wrote in his holy letter,
"When I read in the book of Tehillim the verse 'He redeemed my soul in peace,' etc., I went out in peace, from Hashem is peace."
Regarding the redemption of the Mitteler Rebbe on Yud Kislev,
it is known
that our Nesi'im would recite the daily portion of Tehillim as divided by the days of the month,
and since the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" is in the monthly Tehillim portion for the tenth day of the month,
therefore, on the day of his redemption
(the tenth of Kislev)
he said this verse.
And regarding the redemption of my father-in-law, the Rebbe, on Yud-Beis Tammuz,
it is known
the custom of our Nesi'im that in special times and situations they would add the recitation of the Tehillim portion as divided by the days of the week
(in addition to the monthly Tehillim portion),
and since the date of Yud-Beis Tammuz in the year 5687
(the year of the arrest and redemption)
fell on the third day of the week, and the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" is in the weekly Tehillim portion for the third day of the week,
it is understood,
that the master of the redemption of Yud-Beis Tammuz said this verse on the day of his redemption.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the connection of the Yud Kislev redemption to this verse is even more pronounced than the others, as it recurs annually.
section.t: And it is explained elsewhere,
that the connection of the redemption of Yud Kislev to the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" is
(in one aspect)
even greater than the connection of the redemptions of Yud-Tes Kislev and Yud-Beis Tammuz to this verse,
for since this verse is in the Tehillim portion for the tenth day of the month,
the connection of this verse to
[the redemption of]
Yud Kislev is emphasized every single year.
